content:
Instagram now has a new iPhone-only feature that can automatically create Reels videos. You simply pick your clips and with one tap, a edited version is generated.

However, Meta is being very careful not to offend creators and make them feel like this feature could replace their manual editing skills...

This cautious approach even extends to the feature's name - "First Draft" - implying it only provides a starting point for creation.

The company shared the process and example results in a Threads post.

There's even an option to generate a first draft edit immediately after filming.

You can use this feature in two ways: 1. Open the Reels media library → select at least one clip → tap the "First draft" button at the bottom → review the edit → enter the full editor or publish directly. 2. Open the Instagram camera → film your content → tap the "First draft" button → review the edit → enter the full editor and publish.

Some creators questioned why this feature is in the main Instagram app rather than Edits. The company responded that if needed, it could be offered on both apps in the future. Currently, this feature is only available on the iPhone app, with the Android version expected to roll out later.
